title: The All-in-One Off-Grid Survival Manual: [10-in-1] How to Live Anywhere, Protect Your Fami
description: RELEASED: 300+ DIY Projects to Generate Power, Secure Water, Grow Food, Preserve Supplies, Protect Your Family, and Build True Self-Sufficiency Without Expensive Tools or Prior Experience! What happens when the power grid fails… stores run empty… fuel becomes limited… water systems stop working… or inflation makes everyday living unaffordable? Most people panic because they depend on systems they never learned to live without. This book was built so YOU never have to. Inside this massive 10-in-1 survival and self-sufficiency blueprint , you’ll discover practical step-by-step systems that help ordinary people become more independent, more prepared, and far less vulnerable to emergencies, shortages, blackouts, economic instability, and modern dependence. And unlike most survival books filled with fantasy scenarios, military jargon, or expensive “prepper gear”… This guide focuses on real-world off-grid systems you can actually build, afford, and use. No complicated engineering. No overpriced equipment. No unrealistic survival nonsense. Just practical systems, DIY projects, and field-tested strategies that help you gradually build real self-reliance one step at a time. Inside This Massive 10-in-1 Survival Manual, You’ll Discover: ✅ How to keep the lights on, the water flowing, and food on the table … even when everybody else is panicking ✅ The “silent survival systems” smart families are building NOW before shortages, blackouts, and emergencies hit ✅ The simple DIY setups that can slash your dependence on grocery stores, utility companies, and fragile supply chains ✅ How to turn your home into a self-reliant fortress for power, water, food, security, communication, and survival ✅ The overlooked preparedness mistakes that quietly leave families vulnerable when disaster strik

title: The Off-Grid Survival Projects Handbook, Volume 2: 69 Step-by-Step Projects for Cold Night
description: When the power goes out on a cold night, do you know how to keep the heat in, the water safe, and your family fed? Most survival books start with the big builds. The first bad night does not wait for them. The Off-Grid Survival Projects Handbook, Volume 2 gives you 69 step-by-step projects, ordered the way trouble arrives: first night first, then outward. Most are laid out the same clear way, so you always know what to gather, what it costs, and exactly what to do. Most projects include: A difficulty, time, and cost label up front, so you can pick work that fits your day and your budget A "You will need" list A Safety block that comes before the steps Numbered steps you can follow A labeled diagram so you can see how it goes together Troubleshooting for when something goes wrong, and a Level Up note for when you have the basics Inside you will build the skills that matter most: The first bad night: a utility shutoff station, battery carbon monoxide alarms, fire prevention, downed power lines and flood water, and frozen pipes Heat: heating one room safely, a cold-weather sleep system, window insulation, a chimney and stovepipe inspection, and a rocket mass heater bench Water: hauling, storing, and treating drinking water, a barrel sand and gravel filter, a solar still, a hydraulic ram pump, and a spring box Food: a hay box, sourdough without a fridge, a 3-month pantry, dried food and jerky, dry-pack jars, and a no-power ice box Skills, tools, and land: map and compass, a Stop the Bleed wound kit, a 12-volt battery box, salvage, keeping an edge, a brake-drum forge, grafting, shiitake logs, and a living hedge and windbreak You also get a Scenario Index that sends you to the right projects when a pipe freezes, the water is not safe, the fridge goes off, or a storm is coming

title: Off the Grid: The brand new grumpy sunshine romance set at a breathtaking wilderness retre

No algorithms. No cell service. Time to go completely Off the Grid !✨ When Bea March’s carefully curated life spectacularly unravels during a live-streamed proposal gone wrong, she becomes the internet’s latest viral disaster. Humiliated and desperate to disappear, she escapes to a wilderness retreat in Alaska, where the Wi-Fi is scarce, the mountains are vast and her heeled boots are hopelessly impractical. At a remote lodge run by three rugged brothers, Bea finds herself at odds with Cass Sawyer, the grumpy, closed-off wilderness guide with little patience for a curious city girl who’s hopelessly out of her depth – and only supposed to be passing through. But when Cass is forced to teach her how to survive the wild, Bea proves herself far more resilient than either of them expected. And somewhere between glacier hikes, crackling campfires and endless blue skies, their hostility gives way to an unexpected chemistry… Bea came to Alaska for a great escape. But stranded deep in the wilderness with the one man she thought she couldn’t stand, she’ll have to decide whether she’s willing to risk her heart – and her carefully rebuilt life – on the adventure of a lifetime… Full of emotional small-town romance, unforgettable grumpy heroes and breathtaking wilderness settings, this swoony, slow-burn love story is perfect for fans of K.A. What happens if the power goes down or the grocery stores fail to get supplies? What happens if your access to medical care is cut off and someone in your family needs treatment? title: The Off-Grid Survival Apothecary: 650+ Herbal Remedies, Natural First Aid & Emergency Medi
description: The pharmacy is closed. The roads are out. Your child has a fever, a deep cut, or a cough that will not quit. What do you do in the next hour? Most families have a flashlight and a few cans of food. Very few have a plan for the moment someone gets hurt or sick and help is not coming. The Off-Grid Survival Apothecary is that plan: a calm, practical medicine guide for power outages, storms, evacuations and long supply shortages, written so you can act fast when it matters. 650+ remedies you can actually make Every one of the 655 numbered remedies tells you what to use it for, what you need, how to make it, the dose, who should not use it, and the warning signs that mean you need professional help. Each one carries two ratings: how strong the evidence is (Strong, Moderate or Traditional) and how careful you need to be (Green, Amber or Red). No guesswork, no hype. Inside, you will learn how to: Handle the first hour : triage, CPR, the recovery position, and when to treat, watch or evacuate. Stop serious bleeding with pressure, tourniquets and wound packing, then clean and dress wounds so they heal. Treat burns, sprains, bites, stings and poison ivy with first aid first and herbs second. Get through fevers, flu, coughs, stomach bugs and dehydration , including an oral rehydration drink you can mix from salt and sugar. Ease pain, headaches, toothache and earache when the pharmacy shelves are empty. Calm stress, panic and sleepless nights during weeks of disruption. Care safely for babies, children, pregnant women, seniors and pets , with clear doses and firm rules. Avoid dangerous herb–drug interactions with a quick-check table for common medicines. title: The Lost Skills Off-Grid Handbook: Old-Time Self-Reliance Projects Our Grandparents Knew –
description: Our grandparents could put food by, keep a fire going, mend a coat and read the sky. This handbook teaches those everyday skills the way they are done safely today, one plain step at a time. Each of the 175 skills and step-by-step projects opens with Then , how people did it 100 to 200 years ago, and Now , the safe method you will actually use. Where an old method is simply unsafe, such as open-kettle canning, the book says so and shows what replaced it. What you get Real old-time skills, not prepper filler. No tactical gear, bug-out bags or doomsday talk. Just bread, butter, candles, soap, darning, knots, rain barrels and root cellars. 43 of them are build projects, each with its own labeled diagram. Parts are numbered and labeled; build projects give sizes in inches and feet. 93 black-and-white line illustrations of hand positions, knots and the key features of plants. Exact numbers with sources. Canning times and pressures, bleach doses, safe temperatures, lye rules and electrical limits are each tied to a source listed at the end of the chapter. Most of those sources are public agencies and university Extension services. An Effort rating for Hands, Knees and Back on every skill, so you know before you start how much gripping, kneeling and lifting a job takes. A rating table on every skill: time, cost, difficulty, where (house, apartment or yard) and season. A Pass It Down box in every chapter: one skill to teach, with a job for ages 5–8, ages 9–12 and teens, and a question to ask an older relative. An adult is there for every child's job. The Family Skills Keepsake: an interview guide of 30 questions for a parent or grandparent, plus headings for recording your family's skills, recipes and know-how, the skills you pass down, and a letter to the next generation. title: TOTAL BLACKOUT: The First 72 Hours That Could Save Your Family
description: ⚡ WHAT IF THE POWER WENT OUT… AND NEVER CAME BACK? No electricity. No internet. No running water. No communication. No guarantee that help is coming. Imagine waking up to a world where the power grid has failed, supermarkets are closing, electronic payments have stopped working, and your family depends entirely on the decisions you make next. Would you know what to do during the first 72 hours? In TOTAL BLACKOUT: The First 72 Hours That Could Save Your Family , Daniel Westford reveals practical survival strategies to help you prepare for prolonged power outages, infrastructure failures, and unexpected emergencies. You don't need expensive equipment or years of survival training.
